preamble: A labial stop becomes the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] when a following palatal glide or lateral is absorbed into it (labial palatalization). Southern Bantu turned Proto-Bantu *p before a glide into [ʃ], and Portuguese turned Latin initial pl- into ch, an affricate [tʃ] that later simplified to [ʃ].

examples.note: *p + glide coalesces into [ʃ]; Xhosa has the affricate stage -tsha [tʃʼa]
pl- > [tʃ] > [ʃ]; the affricate survives in northern Portuguese dialects

sources: Nurse, D., & Philippson, G. (Eds.) (2003). The Bantu Languages. Routledge.
Williams, E. B. (1962). From Latin to Portuguese: Historical Phonology and Morphology of the Portuguese Language. 2nd ed. University of Pennsylvania Press.
